title: A circle of running time: outline vs haze
question: Which one reads as a bubble of running time you would want to place, rather than a line drawn over the world?
context_md:
You asked for this: *"They shouldn't be a solid line it blocks too much. I am thinking hazy shimmering aura. Think about how to indicate speed visual."*

Both arms are the same world, the same seed, the same frames, at **speed x8** — the top of the dial, which is where the old look was worst because it added one more hard circle per two steps.

**Look at the filled circle on the right.** The large thin circle around the gnome is the *placement preview* — what SPACE would put down — and it is unchanged in both arms. It is still a hard line, and that is the obvious next thing to soften if you want it softened.

**Watch it move.** Speed is meant to read two ways: how fast the haze pulses (it is not a mapping — the pulse is the world's own clock, so a x8 circle pulses eight times faster because time there really is running eight times faster), and how deep the haze reaches inward, which is the half a still frame keeps. The second card has the four speeds side by side as stills.

**One thing I did not fix, because the file belongs to another session tonight**: above x1 the gnome's own circle disappears from the picture entirely — his warm halo is missing here and the ground under him greys out. That is not new and not the haze; `step_extra_ticks` lifts the player out of the world for the catch-up passes and never puts his circle back, so nothing that draws between two updates can see it. It needs one line in `src/druid/mod.rs`.

items.label: A — outline (current)
items.caption: one hard 1px circle per quickening, plus one more inside it per two steps of the dial

items.label: B — haze (proposed)
items.caption: a per-cell tint in the world pass; nothing is painted over
